'''Sindee''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] member of the [[Hair/Legends|furred]] [[Bimm (furred species)/Legends|Bimm]] [[Species/Legends|species]] who lived during the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. A shrewd businesswoman, she operated a [[Sindee's refueling station|one-woman refueling station]].<ref name="Re-animated" /> Around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]],<ref name="Chronology note">{{SW|url=news/the-droids-re-animated-part-1|series=The Droids Re-Animated|text=Part 1|nolive=1}} establishes that Sindee acquired [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] approximately fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of {{Film|IV}}, which are dated to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] ended up at the [[Space station/Legends|station]] after being ejected there from a [[Starship/Legends|ship]] bound for the [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Ord Gertoth]], and Sindee became their new master. Sindee taught R2-D2 to play [[Dejarik/Legends|dejarik]], but a [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] addiction the businesswoman harbored saw her lose both droids to the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Zevel Hortine]] in a game of [[Liar's Cut/Legends|Liar's Cut]].<ref name="Re-animated" />

==Behind the scenes==
Sindee was first mentioned, albeit unidentified, in the [[1981]] [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio]] episode "[[Rogues, Rebels and Robots]]."<ref name="Rogues">{{SWRadio|Rogues, Rebels and Robots}}</ref> She was later identified by name in "[[The Droids Re-Animated]]," a [[Star Wars Blog|blog]] article written by [[Rich Handley]] and [[Abel G. Peña]] that was posted on [[StarWars.com]] on [[June 13]], [[2013]].<ref name="Re-animated" />
